title: Scaling the Vocabulary of Non-autoregressive Models for Fast Generative Retrieval

problem.claim: Autoregressive generative retrieval has high inference latency and cost, while standard non-autoregressive models reduce these costs but suffer lower retrieval performance because they cannot capture dependencies between target tokens.

gap.claim: The conventional restriction of non-autoregressive target vocabularies to words or sub-words may limit their ability to reduce target-token dependencies.

contributions.claim: PIXNAR expands the target vocabulary of non-autoregressive models to include multi-word entities and common phrases, with up to 5 million tokens.
PIXNAR uses inference optimization strategies to maintain low inference latency despite its larger vocabulary.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present PIXNAR as a novel approach that expands the target vocabulary of non-autoregressive models with multi-word entities and common phrases.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Compared with standard non-autoregressive models at similar latency and cost, PIXNAR improves MRR@10 by 31.0% relatively on MS MARCO.
Compared with standard non-autoregressive models at similar latency and cost, PIXNAR improves Hits@5 by 23.2% on Natural Questions.
Online A/B experiments on a large commercial search engine reportedly show significant increases in clicks and revenue.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generative retrieval reframes information retrieval as constrained generation using autoregressive language models.
Autoregressive methods have high latency and cost, limiting practical applicability.
The paper investigates non-autoregressive models, which reduce latency and cost but lose retrieval performance because they cannot capture target-token dependencies.
PIXNAR expands the non-autoregressive target vocabulary with multi-word entities and common phrases and applies inference optimization.
The authors report benchmark improvements and positive online A/B experiment outcomes.

source_observation.claim: Expanding the target vocabulary with multi-word entities and common phrases is reported to improve non-autoregressive retrieval performance while preserving similar latency and cost.

interpretation.claim: Larger structured output units may reduce dependencies that constrain parallel generation.

application.claim: For generative retrieval systems, evaluate whether phrase- or entity-level output units can improve quality without violating latency and cost targets.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported benchmarks or deployment setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the model architecture, training procedure, or inference optimization details.
The abstract does not provide absolute latency, cost, click, or revenue values.
The abstract does not report statistical significance details or independent verification of the results.
